# Build-vs-Buy Decision Memo

Control area: prod-db-access-least-privilege

## Control as a product

Control: prod-db-access-least-privilege
Owner: M. Okafor
Customers (priority order):
1. Engineer — wants access grants self-service, time-boxed, auto-revoked (invisible)
2. Auditor — wants a durable, dated log proving who had access when, and that it expired
3. Business — wants the breach blast-radius reduced without slowing incident response
Backlog (ranked):
1. 12 standing grants never expire — the actual risk
2. Evidence is a manual quarterly export — toil
3. No alert when a grant outlives its on-call shift — coverage gap
UX target: access auto-granted at shift start, auto-revoked at shift end; the revocation log IS the evidence
Metrics: standing-grant count (target 0), mean grant lifetime, evidence toil hrs/qtr, loss exposure bought down ($/yr)

## Quantified loss exposure

The fixture decomposes the gap into two separately estimated ranges: frequency 0.1-0.6 events/year (how often a standing grant is abused or compromised), and magnitude $300,000-$2,500,000 per event (what one data incident costs in response, notification, and churn). They are estimated separately because different evidence informs each: incident history speaks to frequency; the value at stake speaks to magnitude.

Reference run on the committed fixture (seed 42, 10,000 iterations): mean expected annual loss $493,516/yr; 95th-percentile bad year (the tail) $1,133,873/yr.

The executive underwrites the bad year, not the average: doubling the worst-case magnitude to $5M moved the mean to $934,417 but the p95 tail to $2,240,391 — the tail is where the control earns its budget.

## Seven-stage build/buy/hybrid scoring

UNDERSTAND — BUILD: no vendor knows our on-call model or context.
LOCATE — BUY: the platform integrates IdP/DB/cloud truth sources at scale.
QUERY — BUY: connectors and rate-limit handling are commodity plumbing.
EVALUATE — BUILD: the time-box + on-call rule is OUR policy; a generic check flattens it.
EVIDENCE — HYBRID: vendor store, our schema and retention — no lock-in.
MONITOR — BUY: scheduling and alerting are commodity; the thresholds stay ours.
OWN — BUILD: accountability cannot be outsourced.

## The boundary argument

The vendor owns LOCATE, QUERY, and MONITOR; we own UNDERSTAND, EVALUATE, and OWN, and we run EVIDENCE hybrid (their store, our schema).

Vendor wins: LOCATE across forty SaaS apps — building and maintaining forty OAuth integrations is undifferentiated heavy lifting the platform amortizes across hundreds of customers; our hand-built copy would be worse and slower (textbook NIH).
